candidates.name: FirstRate Data
candidates.notes: Buy once, own the file. Good when you want a fixed historical set rather than a subscription.

candidates.name: Kibot
candidates.notes: Long histories, unadjusted and adjusted variants. Check which you are buying -- the integrity engine will back-adjust splits for you either way.

candidates.name: Interactive Brokers
candidates.cost: free with a funded account plus exchange data fees
candidates.notes: If you already have an IBKR account this is effectively free. Pacing limits make bulk history slow -- fine for topping up, painful for a first pull.

candidates.name: Databento
candidates.cost: pay per GB, tick data is the expensive part
candidates.notes: Already wired in. The only source here with true MBO/MBP order flow for futures. Tick data is one to three orders of magnitude dearer than bars -- the cost notifier says so before every pull.

candidates.name: Barchart
candidates.notes: Broad coverage including agricultural and energy futures that other vendors skip.

candidates.name: CME DataMine
candidates.history: back to the 1970s on some contracts
candidates.notes: Straight from the exchange, so it is the reference other vendors are checked against. Expensive and delivered as bulk files.
